items.t: Terra Nova is the north-west Richmond pocket on Lulu Island, west of No. 1 Road at the end of Westminster Highway, beside the Middle Arm / Sturgeon Bank foreshore. The City plans the same ground as a sub-area in the Thompson planning area — Official Community Plan Schedule 2.2B Thompson (Terra Nova) — and the City Heritage Inventory describes the area as from No. 1 Road westward, with Westminster Highway to the south, the Fraser River to the north and west, and No. 1 Road to the east, including the foreshore outside the dyke.

Where multi-family stock actually concentrates: along Westminster Highway at the pocket's south edge (Mayflower at 3880 Westminster Highway, Sonoma at 3555 Westminster Highway) and on Cornwall Drive inside the pocket (Quilchena Green at 5531 Cornwall Drive). All three verified complexes are townhouse form. The rest of the pocket is detached houses, with farm land in the AG1 / ALR framework to the west and south.
Main roads: Westminster Highway, No. 1 Road and River Road; Terra Nova Rural Park is at the west end of Westminster Highway west of No. 1 Road.

Transit: bus service on No. 1 Road and Westminster Highway connects the pocket to Richmond–Brighouse Station on the Canada Line; no Canada Line station is inside the sub-area. Route-level detail beyond that connection: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Terra Nova

items.t: Age bylaws — SPA ss. 123.1 / 123.2: only a 55-or-older residency bylaw is valid in BC; any younger threshold (for example a "45+" label) cannot be enforced as an age-restriction bylaw under the current Act. Exemptions cover legacy residents, live-in caregivers and (from May 1, 2023) younger spouses/partners and defined children. This is why Quilchena Green's 45+ / 55+ label conflict matters and why it is carried as UNCONFIRMED pending the registered bylaws: if a 45+ figure appears anywhere in older marketing, it is not a lawful age-bylaw threshold today.

Official Community Plan: Richmond Official Community Plan Schedule 2.2B Thompson (Terra Nova) is the sub-area plan for the pocket; the city-wide plan is the City of Richmond 2041 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 9000.

Flood protection and Flood Bylaw 8204: Richmond is protected by a perimeter dike system with drainage pump stations (49 km of dikes, 39 pump stations city-wide), designed for a 1:500 flood event, with dike raising from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres for sea level rise under way; the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204 sets setbacks from a dike right-of-way and bars building below the flood plain construction level in its Schedule B — directly relevant to the Cornwall Drive and Westminster Highway complexes near the dyke.

ALR beside the pocket: Agricultural Land Commission guidance allows one principal residence and, if the regulation conditions are met, one additional residence per parcel in the Agricultural Land Reserve — the rule set for the farm parcels beside the residential pocket, not for the strata complexes themselves.

District energy (ADEU): the Alexandra District Energy Utility serves the West Cambie / Alexandra neighbourhood (Bylaw No. 8641 is framed for buildings within the Alexandra neighbourhood, and the utility operator describes the ADEU system as serving the West Cambie neighbourhood).

Richmond property tax timing: City of Richmond property taxes are due once a year on the first business day of July — Thursday, July 2, 2026 — with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after that date and a further 5% penalty on balances still outstanding after September 1, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Terra Nova

items.t: Quilchena Green is Terra Nova stock, whatever the name suggests.

Two of the three complexes share one builder and one amenity pattern. Mayflower and Sonoma are both Polygon townhouse communities on Westminster Highway with clubhouse / pool / hot tub / gym amenity sets built a year apart (Sonoma 1995; Mayflower 1996/97) — cross-complex comparisons of construction and strata practice are unusually direct here.
The pocket's plan name is not its postal name.

The area's Indigenous name is on the school. Terra Nova was named Spul'u'kwuks by Indigenous Peoples who used it for seasonal fishing camps, and the elementary school inside the pocket carries that name (Spul'u'kwuks Elementary, 5999 Blanshard Drive); Newfoundland fishermen later renamed the area Terra Nova, "new land," and the Terra Nova Cannery operated there into the middle of the 20th century.
Shopping in the pocket is asserted everywhere and verified nowhere official.

Buyers also search "Spul'u'kwuks" (the area's Indigenous name, and the name of the elementary school in the pocket) and "Terra Nova Village."

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: (1) Westminster Highway at the pocket's south edge — Mayflower (3880 Westminster Highway) and Sonoma (3555 Westminster Highway); (2) Cornwall Drive inside the pocket — Quilchena Green (5531 Cornwall Drive); (3) the No. 1 Road east edge — London Mews (6333 No. The rest of the pocket is detached houses, with farm land in the AG1 / ALR framework to the west and south.

Transit and roads: bus service on No. 1 Road and Westminster Highway connects the pocket to Richmond–Brighouse Station on the Canada Line; no Canada Line station and no highway interchange is inside the sub-area. Schools: School District 38 (Richmond) catchments are address-based and the district has no middle-school tier — elementary is Kindergarten to Grade 7 and secondary is Grades 8 to 12. blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Terra Nova

items.t: Form B diligence (all 4 strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern, including Quilchena Green's age-bylaw wording.

Depreciation reports / CRF minimum: since July 1, 2024, strata corporations with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, not deferrable by vote — all four counted complexes are well over the threshold on their published forms (Quilchena Green 91 units, London Mews 66 units; Mayflower and Sonoma unit counts UNCONFIRMED but plainly multi-building strata communities). Since Nov 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go to the contingency reserve fund.

Fee-simple homes (the pocket's detached stock): NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees — diligence is title, municipal rules (Zoning Bylaw 8500) and any registered covenants only, stated plainly. There is no verified fee-simple townhouse complex in Terra Nova; the fee-simple product here is detached houses and ALR farm parcels, which follow different rules again (below).

City zoning / OCP (Richmond — standing program figures): Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500, Official Community Plan Bylaw 9000 (the City of Richmond 2041 OCP), Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204. The sub-area plan is OCP Schedule 2.2B Thompson (Terra Nova). Quilchena Green carries RTL 1 zoning on its MLS record. For farm land beside the pocket, Agriculture (AG1) in Zoning Bylaw 8500 Section 14.1 provides for farming and compatible uses consistent with the Agricultural Land Reserve, one principal dwelling unit per lot, and a secondary suite as a secondary use; subdivision in the ALR is not permitted unless approved by the Agricultural Land Commission, and where that approval is not required the minimum lot area is 2.0 ha; single detached housing is not to be built on a lot under 828.0 m² in that zone.

items.t: Quilchena Green is Terra Nova stock, whatever the name suggests. Its home count is here.
Its age label disagrees with itself across time. A 2016 MLS sheet records 45+; current listings record 55+.

Two of the four complexes share one builder and one amenity pattern. Mayflower and Sonoma are both Polygon townhouse communities on Westminster Highway (1995–1997 era) with the same resort-style set — clubhouse, outdoor pool, hot tub, gym — so a buyer cross-shopping them is really comparing floorplans, yards and strata health, not amenity lists. Basis: above.

The pocket's plan name is not its postal name. The City plans this ground as Thompson (Terra Nova) — OCP Schedule 2.2B — and the Heritage Inventory lists its planning area as Thompson, while the board and the market call it Terra Nova.

The rural park is a no-dogs park. Terra Nova Rural Park, 2631 Westminster Highway, is a 63-acre site with trails, the Adventure Play Environment and the Sharing Farm on the Pacific Flyway beside the Sturgeon Bank Wildlife Management Area — and it is a NO DOGS ALLOWED area under Animal Control Bylaw 8612, which matters to dog-owning buyers who assume dyke-side living means dyke-side dog walks. (The West Dyke Trail itself runs from the park south to Garry Point Park.)

Care anchors are in the wider Thompson / City Centre area, not the pocket. Thompson Community Centre is at 5151 Granville Avenue; the nearest hospital is Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway (Vancouver Coastal Health), and Richmond City Centre Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #110, 4671 No. 3 Road; the nearest full library branch named on an official source is Richmond Public Library Brighouse (Main) Branch, 100-7700 Minoru Gate — there is no library branch in the pocket.

Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established house lots: single-detached houses in the residential pocket east of the rural park, the documented base form alongside the ALR farm parcels.

Serviced position, as stated: Terra Nova homes are on City water and sewer services in the residential pocket. Added-unit position (non-ALR lots): the City states Richmond allows at least one secondary suite and/or an accessory dwelling unit per lot, with Bill 44 small-scale multi-unit minimums of 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units on larger lots — the ALR farm lots follow the ALR framework instead (below).

blocks.text: ALR farm land

items.t: AG1 framework, as the bylaw states it: for farm land beside the pocket, Agriculture (AG1) in Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500 Section 14.1 provides for farming and compatible uses consistent with the Agricultural Land Reserve, one principal dwelling unit per lot, and a secondary suite as a secondary use. Subdivision in the ALR is not permitted unless approved by the Agricultural Land Commission, and where that approval is not required the minimum lot area is 2.0 ha; single detached housing is not to be built on a lot under 828.0 m² in that zone.

ALR vs non-ALR split: the pocket's house lots are non-ALR residential ground; the farm land to the west and south is ALR ground under AG1. No parcel count or percentage split for Terra Nova is stated in the research — none is invented; ALR status for a specific parcel is confirmed on ALC mapping.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Terra Nova

items.t: OCP — City of Richmond 2041 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 9000: with Schedule 2.2B Thompson (Terra Nova) as the sub-area plan listed by the City for this ground.

Zoning — Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500: residential pocket lots under their parcel zones (confirmed lot by lot); farm land under Agriculture AG1, Section 14.1 (one principal dwelling per lot, secondary suite as a secondary use, 2.0 ha subdivision minimum where ALC approval is not required, no single detached housing on a lot under 828.0 m² in that zone).

SSMUH / added units as the City states it (non-ALR lots only): at least one secondary suite and/or accessory dwelling unit per lot, with Bill 44 minimums of 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units on larger lots. AG1 farm lots follow the ALR framework below instead — do not price SSMUH potential into an ALR parcel.

ALR rules (the farm-land framework): subdivision in the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC guidance allows one principal residence and, if the regulation conditions are met, one additional residence per parcel — caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

Flood / dike diligence — Bylaw 8204: dike setbacks and the flood plain construction level (Schedule B) apply; the pocket sits behind the 1:500-design perimeter system with dike raising under way. Get the parcel-level position early on west- and north-edge purchases.
Heritage diligence: the Terra Nova Heritage Area is on the City Heritage Inventory — heritage status is a lot-level diligence item for parcels in or beside the inventoried area.

Strata block — applies to the built townhouse ground (Quilchena Green and peers), NOT to bare land here: Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (covenant-based rental obligations, where registered, are a separate position —); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children).

Richmond property taxes: due once a year on the first business day of July — Thursday, July 2, 2026 — with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after that date and a further 5% penalty on balances still outstanding after September 1, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Terra Nova

items.t: "Terra Nova" means "new land" — and the older name is on the school: Indigenous Peoples used Terra Nova for seasonal fishing camps during salmon and sturgeon runs and the area was named Spul'u'kwuks; Newfoundland fishermen later renamed it Terra Nova, and the Terra Nova Cannery operated there until the middle of the 20th century. The elementary school in the pocket still carries the Spul'u'kwuks name.

The rural park is a no-dogs park: Terra Nova Rural Park (63 acres, Sharing Farm, Adventure Play Environment, Pacific Flyway trails) is a NO DOGS ALLOWED area under Animal Control Bylaw 8612 — a real factor for dog-owning buyers pricing dyke-side lots, and one listing copy rarely mentions.

The foreshore is inside the area description: the City Heritage Inventory's Terra Nova description includes the foreshore outside the dyke to the north and west, beside the Sturgeon Bank Wildlife Management Area — edge "land" there is foreshore and habitat ground under the dike framework, not buildable lot area.

The No. 1 Road corner has been "proposed" since 2012: the only development record at the pocket's east edge is the 2012 panel note for 6011/6031 No. 1 Road — fourteen years on, its status is still UNCONFIRMED and it is counted in no program total. Price the corner as it stands today, not as the proposal. Basis: above.

Page-statement check for this area. Approved page claims, where a live page states them, are the settled set only: REALTOR since 2015; 10 straight years in the FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points for 2025 and 2026 YTD; more than $500M in sales.

faq.q: How is Terra Nova reached by transit?
faq.a: Bus service on No. 1 Road and Westminster Highway connects the pocket to Richmond–Brighouse Station on the Canada Line; there is no Canada Line station inside the sub-area.

faq.q: Can a farm parcel beside the pocket have a second dwelling?
faq.a: Agricultural Land Commission guidance allows one principal residence and, if the regulation conditions are met, one additional residence per parcel in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and Richmond AG1 zoning also lists a secondary suite as a secondary use.

faq.q: What flood protection applies in Terra Nova?
faq.a: The City states Richmond has a perimeter dike system with drainage pump stations, designed for a 1:500 event, with dike raising from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres under way; Bylaw 8204 also sets dike setbacks and a flood plain construction level.

Terra Nova Rural Park, 2631 Westminster Highway — a 63-acre site with trails, the Adventure Play Environment and the Sharing Farm, on the Pacific Flyway beside the Sturgeon Bank Wildlife Management Area — plus the West Dyke Trail running south from the park to Garry Point Park.

faq.q: Can I buy an apartment condo in Terra Nova?
faq.a: No verified strata apartment building was found. Terra Nova's strata stock is three townhouse complexes — Quilchena Green (5531 Cornwall Drive, 91 homes, built 1992), Mayflower (3880 Westminster Highway, Polygon) and Sonoma (3555 Westminster Highway, Polygon, built 1995).

Current listings describe a 55+ requirement (one occupant / one owner on title at 55+, other occupants permitted), while the earlier research program recorded a 45+/55+ conflict; under the Strata Property Act only a 55+ bylaw is valid in any event. faq.a: Published as pets allowed with restrictions; the current listing's bylaw summary records cats and dogs OK to a maximum of one. Confirm against the registered bylaws — pet bylaws remain enforceable in BC.

There are no verified fee-simple townhouse complexes and no apartment condos in the pocket. Basis: above.
